extraction_tips: This is page 1 of the ACORD 126 Commercial General Liability Section, 2016 edition.
Capture the edition year '2016' and the page number '1 of 2' from the form header or footer if printed.
The date field in the header is the application or quote date; leave it null if no date appears.
ui_tips: Display the form title 'Commercial General Liability Section' and edition '2016' clearly at the top of the UI.
Show the current page number (1 of 2) and overall navigation consistently with other ACORD forms.
Place the header date field next to other policy header fields to match the PDF layout.

extraction_tips: From the header block on page 1, extract AGENCY, CARRIER, NAIC CODE, POLICY NUMBER / QUOTE, EFFECTIVE DATE (MM/DD/YYYY), and APPLICANT (First Named Insured) exactly as they appear.
If the form includes a single line such as 'COMMERCIAL GENERAL LIABILITY CLAIMS MADE', capture that full text into COVERAGE FORM DESCRIPTION.

Capture the COMMERCIAL GENERAL LIABILITY coverage checkbox and the OCCURRENCE/CLAIMS-MADE basis checkboxes (to the left of their labels) into the COMMERCIAL_GENERAL_LIABILITY, CLAIMS_MADE, and OCCURRENCE fields.
Do not infer or rearrange header values; if a field is blank on the PDF, leave the corresponding metadata value null.
ui_tips: Group policy identification (carrier, policy number, effective/expiration dates) with the main coverage checkboxes in a single panel.
Align checkboxes visually with their descriptive labels as shown on the ACORD 126 2016 PDF.
Use helper text or tooltips to clarify occurrence vs claims-made options, mirroring the wording on the form.

extraction_tips: From the LIMITS grid on page 1, extract the limit amounts for GENERAL AGGREGATE, PRODUCTS-COMPLETED OPERATIONS AGGREGATE, PERSONAL & ADVERTISING INJURY, EACH OCCURRENCE, DAMAGE TO PREMISES RENTED TO YOU, MEDICAL EXPENSE, and EMPLOYEE BENEFITS.
Strip out currency symbols and commas when interpreting the numeric values, but keep the raw text in this metadata field.
From the same block, capture PREM/OPS, PRODUCTS, OTHER, and TOTAL premium amounts into the premium-related fields.
If any limit or premium cell is blank on the form, leave the corresponding field null.
ui_tips: Render limits and premiums in a table layout that mirrors the ACORD 126 2016 grid.
Keep limit labels (e.g., 'GENERAL AGGREGATE', 'EACH OCCURRENCE') clearly visible next to their values.
Use numeric-style inputs for limit and premium values while preserving raw string formatting in the stored data.

extraction_tips: Extract deductible amounts for PROPERTY DAMAGE, BODILY INJURY, and any OTHER deductible types shown in the DEDUCTIBLES section.
Copy deductible values exactly as printed, including any 'PER CLAIM' or 'PER OCCURRENCE' notation, into the corresponding fields.
If a deductible type is not listed on the form, leave its field null rather than guessing.
ui_tips: Display deductible types and amounts in a compact grid beneath the limits and premiums section.
Allow free-form or numeric entry for deductible values to support both flat amounts and percentages.
Use labels consistent with the ACORD 126 2016 wording so users can easily match the PDF.

extraction_tips: From the CLAIMS-MADE section, extract retroactive dates and YES/NO answers for exclusions, tail coverage, or similar questions.
Record retroactive dates in MM/DD/YYYY format if present; leave them null if not shown.
Map each YES/NO checkbox to a boolean-style value and leave unchecked options null or false.
ui_tips: Group all claims-made questions and retroactive date fields together under a clearly labeled panel.
Use radio buttons or toggle controls for YES/NO responses to mimic the checkbox behavior on the PDF.
Place date pickers immediately next to their labels, keeping the left-to-right order from the form.

extraction_tips: From the Employee Benefits Liability section, extract limits per employee, aggregate limits, deductibles, and any employee counts that are shown.
If the 2016 form includes a retroactive date for employee benefits, capture it exactly as printed.
Leave these fields null if the Employee Benefits section is blank or not requested.
ui_tips: Render Employee Benefits Liability as an optional block following the main CLAIMS MADE and DEDUCTIBLES sections.
Allow this block to be left empty without validation errors when EBL coverage does not apply.
Use labels and helper text that clearly indicate these values are specific to Employee Benefits Liability.
